description: Neo4j bidirectional converter — lossless round-trip between the canonical TSV schema and a Neo4j property graph: bulk seed via neo4j-admin import, incremental updates via LOAD CSV, export back to TSV via APOC, with a round-trip test proving TSV -> Neo4j -> TSV is byte-stable, plus schema constraints and example Cypher.

userStories.title: Add the Neo4j converter module and optional dependency
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the neo4j driver wired in optionally so the converter is isolated from core.
acceptanceCriteria: Add an optional 'neo4j' extra in pyproject.toml pulling the official neo4j Python driver
Create src/culturescrape/neo4j/__init__.py with a connection helper reading URI/user/password from env or config
Connection helper fails with a clear message when the driver extra is not installed
Tests pass (pytest) for config parsing with the driver mocked
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Generate neo4j-admin import header/argument mapping from canonical TSV
userStories.description: As a user, I want the bulk-import command derived from my TSV so seeding a fresh DB is one step.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a directory of nodes/*.tsv and edges/*.tsv, generate the neo4j-admin import invocation with correct --nodes/--relationships args and --delimiter set to tab

Verify our headers (csid:ID, :LABEL, :START_ID, :END_ID, :TYPE, typed properties) are already valid neo4j-admin headers; if any transformation is needed, write transformed copies rather than mutating originals
Emit the command to a script file and print it; do not require a live DB to generate it
Tests pass (pytest) asserting the generated command references every node and edge file with correct flags
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Implement LOAD CSV incremental import
userStories.description: As a user, I want to add/update data into an existing graph so the DB stays current without a rebuild.
acceptanceCriteria: Generate parameterized Cypher using LOAD CSV WITH HEADERS and FIELDTERMINATOR '\t' that MERGEs nodes on csid and MERGEs relationships on (:START_ID,:END_ID,:TYPE)
MERGE semantics ensure re-running the same import does not duplicate nodes or edges (idempotent)
Typed property columns are coerced to int/float/string per the header suffix
Tests pass (pytest) generating the Cypher and asserting MERGE (not CREATE) is used for both nodes and edges
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Create schema constraints and indexes
userStories.description: As a user, I want a unique constraint on csid so the graph enforces identity and imports are fast.
acceptanceCriteria: Generate Cypher creating a uniqueness constraint on csid and indexes on wikidata_qid and name
Constraint creation is idempotent (IF NOT EXISTS)
Provide a command to apply constraints to a connected DB
Tests pass (pytest) generating the expected constraint/index Cypher
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Implement APOC-based export from Neo4j back to TSV
userStories.description: As a user, I want to pull the graph back into canonical TSV so the round-trip is closed.
acceptanceCriteria: Use apoc.export.csv.* (configured with tab delimiter) or driver-side cursor export to write nodes/*.tsv and edges/*.tsv grouped by label/type
Exported files use the canonical headers and the canonical sort order (csid; START_ID,END_ID,TYPE)
Provenance and typed columns survive export with correct type suffixes
Tests pass (pytest) against a mocked driver returning fixture rows, asserting exported files match the canonical schema
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Prove the round-trip is lossless
userStories.description: As a user, I want a guarantee that TSV -> Neo4j -> TSV does not lose or mangle data.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a round-trip test: load a fixture TSV dataset, import to a Neo4j test instance (or a faithful in-memory/driver fake), export back, and assert byte-equality with the sorted original
Any unavoidable transformation (e.g. property ordering) is normalized before comparison and documented
The test covers nodes with multiple labels, multi-value fields, and BCE dates
Tests pass (pytest) for the round-trip
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Add a to-neo4j / from-neo4j CLI
userStories.description: As a user, I want two commands so importing and exporting are turnkey.
acceptanceCriteria: Add `culturescrape to-neo4j <dir> [--mode admin|loadcsv]` and `culturescrape from-neo4j --out <dir>`
to-neo4j generates the admin-import script or runs LOAD CSV against a connected DB per --mode
from-neo4j exports the connected DB to canonical TSV
Tests pass (pytest) invoking both CLIs with the driver mocked
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Ship example Cypher queries for the four dimensions
userStories.description: As a user, I want ready queries so I can explore the graph immediately after import.
acceptanceCriteria: Add cypher/ examples: shortest cultural path between two entities, all entities contemporary with X, everything ORIGINATES_FROM a region, a language-family DESCENDS_FROM tree
Each query has a comment explaining inputs and expected shape
Queries parse against the constraint/label schema (validated with a Cypher linter or driver explain on a test DB)
Tests pass (pytest) checking each query file is non-empty and references only defined labels/types
Lint passes (ruff)

userStories.title: Document the Neo4j workflow
userStories.description: As a user, I want clear docs so I can seed, update, export, and query without guesswork.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/neo4j.md covers: when to use admin-import vs LOAD CSV, the constraint setup, export, the round-trip guarantee, and the example queries
Include exact commands for a local Neo4j instance
Document the APOC + apoc.export.file_enabled configuration prerequisite
Tests pass (pytest) for any doctested snippet
Lint passes (ruff)
